explanation: Give everyone one bonus. A left-to-right pass enforces each left-neighbor constraint; a right-to-left pass raises bonuses only where the right-neighbor constraint demands it. The maximum of these lower bounds is the minimum valid allocation.
timeComplexity: O(n) Two-pass variants visit each employee twice; heap variants remove n employees at logarithmic cost.
spaceComplexity: O(n) Every version retains n bonus values; heap variants additionally retain n employee entries.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: The forward pass gives the least bonuses satisfying every rising left-neighbor constraint. The backward pass raises bonuses only to satisfy rising right-neighbor constraints. Every valid solution must meet both lower bounds, so taking their maximum at each position is feasible and minimal.
walkthrough: For productivity [2,5,3], start at [1,1,1]. The forward pass raises the middle bonus to 2; the reverse pass needs no further increase. The minimum total is 1+2+1=4.
edgeCases: Equal productivity creates no strict bonus requirement.
Strictly decreasing sequences are handled by the reverse pass.
Every employee receives at least one.
